What is the atomic number of Boron?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
In what year was Elon Musk born?
Elon Musk: Elon Reeve Musk (EE-lon; born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and former public official who is the CEO and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX.
In what year was Radium discovered?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
In what year was Copper discovered?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.

In which country is Minamata disease?

Who is credited with discovering Thorium?
Thorium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
Who is credited with discovering Cauchy–Schwarz inequality?
Cauchy–Schwarz inequality: Viktor Bunyakovsky. It is considered one of the most important and widely used inequalities in mathematics.
Who is credited with discovering Phosphorus?
Phosphorus: Hennig Brand. Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
Formed by the angle of thyroid cartilage around the voice box, this neck protrusion becomes a prominent secondary sex characteristic in most men during puberty — what is it commonly called?
Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.
Given by mouth, IV, or directly into bone marrow, which antiarrhythmic medication treats conditions like ventricular tachycardia but risks serious lung and thyroid side effects?
Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication used to treat and prevent a number of types of cardiac dysrhythmias.
This emotion is defined by dread over events that haven't happened yet, distinguishing it from fear, which responds to a threat that's already present. What is it?
Anxiety is an emotion characterized by an unpleasant state of inner turmoil and includes feelings of dread over anticipated events.
These large Old World monkeys come in six distinct species, each native to a different region of Africa, with one species also found on the Arabian Peninsula — what primate is it?
Baboon are primates comprising the genus Papio, one of the 23 genera of Old World monkeys, in the family Cercopithecidae.
First coined in 1919 by Hungarian engineer Károly Ereky, this multidisciplinary field harnesses living organisms like bacteria and yeast to make products and services. What field is it?

Biotechnology is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of natural sciences and engineering sciences to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.

He won a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physics for an effect he discovered in 1962 while still a Cambridge Ph.D. student — then later turned, controversially, to Transcendental Meditation. Which physicist is he?
Brian Josephson (born 4 January 1940) is a British theoretical physicist and emeritus professor at the University of Cambridge.
Bordered by Aquila, Sagittarius, and Aquarius in the sky's watery region, this half-goat, half-fish zodiac figure is the tiniest of the twelve — which constellation?
Capricornus is one of the constellations of the zodiac.
Known as garbanzo, chana or Bengal gram, this protein-rich legume is mashed into hummus and fried into falafel, with its oldest remains found in Syria — what is it?
Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is an annual legume of the family Fabaceae, subfamily Faboideae, cultivated for its edible seeds.
More closely related to lungfish and land vertebrates than to ordinary ray-finned fish, this ancient lobe-finned fish survives today as a single genus with just two known species — which fish?
Coelacanth are an ancient group of lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii) in the class Actinistia.

This interdisciplinary field, whose name combines a Latin word for 'accusation' with a Greek suffix meaning 'study of,' draws on sociology, psychology, economics, and law to examine crime and deviant behavior. What field is this?
Criminology (from Latin crimen, 'accusation', and Ancient Greek -, -logia, from logos, 'word, reason') is the interdisciplinary study of crime and deviant behaviour.
This annual herb in the celery family, native to North Africa and West Asia, is grown across Eurasia for both its feathery leaves and its seeds, both used to flavor food — what herb is it?
Dill (Anethum graveolens) is an annual herb in the celery family Apiaceae.

Distinguished by permanently erect front fangs and a habit of rearing up while flaring a neck flap, which family of mostly venomous snakes ranges from an 18 cm white-lipped species to a nearly 6-metre giant?
Elapidae (commonly known as elapids, from Ancient) is a family of snakes characterized by their permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth.

This genus of 700-plus flowering trees gets its name from Greek words meaning 'well covered' — a nod to the little cap fused over its stamens — and most species are native to Australia. The leafy 'gum trees' in question are which?
Eucalyptus is a genus of more than 700 species of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
Found at the terminal end of the limb in many vertebrates, this weight-bearing anatomical structure enables locomotion and is typically made up of multiple bony segments — what is it?
Foot (pl.: feet) is an anatomical structure found in many vertebrates. The plural form feet is an instance of i-mutation.

Sometimes called the 'lesser apes' to distinguish them from chimpanzees, gorillas, and orangutans, these smaller, tailless primates live in forests from eastern Bangladesh through Southeast Asia and don't build nests — what are they?
Gibbon are apes in the family Hylobatidae (hylobatids).
This flatfish's English name blends words for 'holy' and 'flat fish,' a nod to its place on the Catholic holy-day menu. Which bottom-dwelling fish?
Halibut is the common name for three species of flatfish in the family of right-eye flounders.
Nesting monogamously in tree cavities across Africa, Asia, and Melanesia, these birds are unique for having their first two neck vertebrae fused solid — which birds?
Hornbill are birds found in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia and Melanesia of the family Bucerotidae.

Co-creator of the breakthrough neural network AlexNet and a contributor to landmark AI systems including GPT and AlphaGo, this computer scientist has won a major deep-learning research award three years running — who is he?
Ilya Sutskever (born 1986) is a computer scientist who specializes in machine learning.
This American psychiatrist and Communist Party USA member is best remembered today for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer — who was she?
Jean Tatlock (February 21, 1914 - January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
Drawing on physiology, biomechanics, and neuropsychology, this scientific discipline studies human body movement and underpins fields from sports psychology to physical therapy — what is it?
Kinesiology (from Ancient Greek (knsis) 'movement' and - -loga 'study of') is the scientific study of human body movement.
This German-born American businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, launching his San Francisco firm in 1853 — who is he?
Levi Strauss (STROWSS; born Lb Strau,; February 26, 1829 - September 26, 1902) was a German-born American businessman who founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans.
The sole species in its genus, this South Chinese fruit has a sweet, mildly tart flavor and a distinctive rose-like floral aroma — name it?
Lychee (US also) are the fruit of the tree Litchi chinensis, the sole member of the genus Litchi, part of the soapberry family, Sapindaceae.
This genus of flowering plants belongs to the chamomile tribe of the sunflower family, and several of its species go by the folk name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Matricaria is a genus of flowering plants in the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family.
Touch this creeping legume's compound leaves and they fold inward within seconds, only reopening minutes later — a textbook example of rapid plant movement. What plant is it?

Mimosa pudica (also called sensitive plant, sleepy grass, sleepy plant, action plant, humble plant, touch-me-not, touch-and-die, shame plant or shy plant) is a creeping annual or perennial flowering plant of the pea/legume family Fabaceae.
Developed under a hypersonic flight program in the late 1990s, three single-use examples of this scramjet aircraft were built, the first destroyed in a 2001 test flight — which record holder is it?
NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Built from proteins, DNA, and RNA around specific chromosomal regions, this nuclear structure is being studied as a target for cancer chemotherapy — what is it?
Nucleolus (pl.: nucleoli) is the largest structure in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
Founded as a science by Georges Cuvier in 1796, when he demonstrated evidence for extinction, this field studies prehistoric life mainly through fossils — what's the discipline?
Paleontology is the scientific study of the life of the past, mainly but not exclusively through the study of fossils.
Which management theorist and educator's writings on organizing business, government, and nonprofit sectors made him one of the most influential thinkers on modern management?

Peter Drucker (November 19, 1909 - November 11, 2005) was an Austrian American management consultant, educator, and author, whose writings contributed to the philosophical and practical foundations of modern management theory.
This genus of single-celled parasites moves from mosquito to human bloodstream, destroying red blood cells and causing a disease with recurring fevers — what is this genus called?
Plasmodium is a genus of unicellular eukaryotes that are obligate parasites of vertebrates and insects.
Classified into acute, chronic, and pelvic pain syndrome subtypes, this condition doesn't always match its name's literal meaning of organ swelling — which condition?
Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.

This bird of prey now breeds only in Europe, though it once also ranged across West Asia and Northwest Africa, with northern populations historically wintering as far as western Africa — what bird is it?
Red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
This root vegetable — a hybrid of cabbage and a related turnip-like plant — goes by different names in North America and Britain, and is often confused for a big turnip. What is it?
Rutabaga (North American English) or swede (British English and some Commonwealth English) is a root vegetable, a form of Brassica napus (which also includes rapeseed).
This Soviet rocket engineer led the early development of his country's space program and designed the R-7, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile — who is he?
Sergei Korolev was Soviet aerospace engineer (1907–1966).

Barred from a formal education, she learned mathematics from her father's library and wrote to Gauss under the male pseudonym 'Monsieur Le Blanc,' later winning a Paris Academy prize for her work on elasticity. Which French mathematician was she?
Sophie Germain (1 April 1776 - 27 June 1831) was a French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.
Developed from an earlier design, this variable-sweep-wing Soviet fighter-bomber served from 1967 to 1990 and was exported in variants like the Su-22 — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-17 (NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
A metabolite of caffeine processed in the liver, this bitter alkaloid is the main one in the cacao plant and turns up in chocolate, tea, and kola nuts. What is it?
Theobromine is the principal alkaloid of Theobroma cacao (cacao plant).
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
Its wild form is dioecious while domesticated versions bear hermaphrodite flowers — this Mediterranean-native plant is the ancestor of nearly all wine and table varieties — what species?

Vitis vinifera is a species of flowering plant, native to the Mediterranean region, Central Europe, and southwestern Asia, from Morocco and Portugal north to southern Germany and east to northern Iran.
Which East Asian citrus fruit, believed to have originated in central China as a hybrid of mandarin orange and ichang papeda, is now also grown in New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Europe?
Yuzu (Citrus junos, from Japanese or) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
Native to Africa and Yemen, this drought-resistant tree species has individuals radiocarbon-dated to over 1,275 years old — what is it?
Adansonia digitata: Species of plant native to Africa.
Brother of a concert pianist and son of an astronomer, this Russian mathematician built the foundational theory of stability in dynamical systems — who was he?
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this white crystalline salt is mildly acidic in solution and is used as both a fertilizer and food additive — which compound?
Ammonium chloride: Chemical compound. Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as [NH4]Cl.
Useless against the cold, the flu, or any fungus, this kind of medicine works only by killing or stalling bacteria — what is it called?
Antibiotic: Antimicrobial substance active against bacteria.
Dubbed the 'Prophet of the Space Age,' this English science fiction author co-wrote the screenplay for 2001: A Space Odyssey and formed sci-fi's 'Big Three' with Heinlein and Asimov — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke: British science fiction writer (1917–2008)
Discovered by Robert Koch in 1876, this rod-shaped microbe was the first ever shown experimentally to cause disease, providing the earliest evidence for germ theory — which organism?
This flowering plant's cultivated varieties include a sugar-producing root crop, the crimson garden vegetable known as beetroot, and the leafy green called chard — what species is it?
Beta vulgaris: Species of flowering plant. Beta vulgaris (beet) is a species of flowering plant in the subfamily Betoideae of the family Amaranthaceae.
A twinjet successor to a trijet predecessor, this American narrow-body airliner entered commercial service with Eastern Air Lines on New Year's Day 1983. Which aircraft?
Too small to fuse hydrogen but massive enough to briefly burn deuterium, these objects between 13 and 80 Jupiter masses cool over time through spectral classes M, L, T, and Y — what are they called?
Cultivated since China's Song Dynasty and boasting thousands of ornamental cultivars, which flowering shrub from the tea family is native to forests of China and Japan?
Camellia japonica: Species of flowering plant.
Nicknamed the pudding-pipe tree, this Fabaceae-family plant is the national tree of Thailand and doubles as the state flower of Kerala and Delhi — which species?

Cassia fistula: Species of flowering plant. Cassia fistula, also known as golden shower, purging cassia, Indian laburnum, kani konna, or pudding-pipe tree, is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae.
Capable of sprinting up to 104 km/h, this spotted big cat is the fastest land animal alive, sporting black tear-like streaks down its face and a flexible spine built for speed — which animal?
Cheetah: Large feline of the genus Acinonyx.
Dubbed the 'father of information theory,' this polymath was the first to apply Boolean algebra to digital circuits and helped found the field of artificial intelligence — who is he?

Nocturnal and marked with narrow white crossbands on a bluish-black body, this South Asian snake's potent neurotoxic venom places it among the region's 'Big Four' most dangerous species — which snake?
Common krait: Species of snake. The common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
These feather-gilled freshwater crustaceans share their taxonomic order with lobsters and turn up in everything from brooks to rice paddies — what are they?
Crayfish: Freshwater crustaceans. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
Most genera in this family of armored, burrowing mammals are extinct — only one genus survives today, with eight living species — which family?

This widely used polar aprotic solvent dissolves both polar and nonpolar compounds, mixes with water, and — once absorbed through the skin — leaves a curious garlic-like taste in the mouth. Which organosulfur compound is it?
Dimethyl sulfoxide: Organosulfur chemical compound used as a solvent.
This German-born British economist championed 'human-scale, appropriate technology' in his 1973 book, later ranked among the 100 most influential books since World War II — who was he?
E. F. Schumacher: British statistician and economist (1911–1977)
This branch of biology and medicine studies the glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream, governing everything from growth to mood and metabolism — what is it called?
Endocrinology: Branch of medicine pertaining to the endocrine system.
Commonly called spurge, this giant plant genus includes the popular Christmas poinsettia and a thorny succulent nicknamed 'crown of thorns' — which genus is it?
A founder of modern topology who also wrote under the playful pen name "Paul Mongré," this German mathematician — Jewish and facing deportation — died by suicide with his family in 1942. Who was he?
Felix Hausdorff: German mathematician (1868–1942). Hausdorff was Jewish, and life became difficult for him and his family after the Kristallnacht of 1938.
This double-layered fold of skin covering the glans is attached by an elastic band called the frenulum and is typically fused in place at birth — what is it?
Foreskin: Retractable fold of skin which covers and protects the glans of the penis.
Nicknamed the 'stomach flu' in the US and Canada, this inflammation of the gut is most often caused in kids by rotavirus and in adults by norovirus — what is it?
Gastroenteritis: Inflammation of the stomach and small intestine.
Occurring mainly in the liver, this metabolic pathway builds new glucose from non-carbohydrate sources to help prevent low blood sugar — what is it called?
Credited as the inventor of radio, this Italian engineer shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics and later set up Vatican Radio for Pope Pius XI — who is he?
Guglielmo Marconi: Italian radio-frequency engineer and inventor (1874–1937)
Native to Africa south of the Sahara, this domesticated bird has since been introduced everywhere from the West Indies to Australia — which species?
Helmeted guinea fowl: Species of bird. The helmeted guinea fowl (Numida meleagris) is the best known of the guinea fowl bird family, Numididae, and the only member of the genus Numida.
Belonging to the genus Apis, this eusocial insect builds perennial nests of hexagonal wax cells and stores surplus food as a prized sweet — which creature is it?
This psychiatric state brings a surge of energy, euphoria, and a reduced need for sleep — milder than its more severe cousin because it doesn't significantly impair daily functioning — what is it?

Also known by names meaning 'water spinach' and 'kangkung,' this semi-aquatic tropical vegetable was likely first domesticated in Southeast Asia and thrives with barely any care near waterways — which plant is it?
Ipomoea aquatica: Species of plant. Ipomoea aquatica, commonly known as water spinach or kangkung, is a semi-aquatic, tropical plant grown as a vegetable for its tender shoots.
With Emmanuelle Charpentier, this Berkeley biochemist proposed in 2012 that CRISPR-Cas9 could edit genomes — work that won them the 2020 Nobel in Chemistry; who is she?
Jennifer Doudna: American biochemist and Nobel laureate (born 1964)
Nicknamed the 'miracle leaf' and 'life plant,' this Madagascar-native succulent sprouts tiny new plantlets right along the edges of its leaves — which species?

Kalanchoe pinnata: Succulent plant native to Madagascar. Kalanchoe pinnata, commonly known as cathedral bells, air plant, life plant, miracle leaf, and love bush, is a succulent plant native to Madagascar.

Native to the tropical Americas, this flowering shrub was carried to Europe by Dutch explorers and later brought to Goa by the Portuguese, becoming a notorious invasive weed across some 50 countries — which plant?
Lantana camara: Species of plant. Lantana camara (common lantana) is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family (Verbenaceae), native to the tropics of the Americas.
Named after the Italian word for lemon, this citrus-scented compound comes in two mirror-image forms — one smelling of oranges, the other like pine — what is it?

This fibrous gourd, edible only when picked young, becomes a scrubbing sponge once fully ripened — and one grown in Graham, NC, broke the world heaviest record in October 2025 at 11 lb 3.3 oz. What is it?
Native to the Malay Peninsula and Borneo, this tropical fruit hides sweet, tangy white flesh beneath a deep reddish-purple rind — which fruit?
Mangosteen: Tropical evergreen tree with edible fruit.
Isolated in 1958 from cow pineal glands because it could lighten frog skin, this nighttime brain hormone turned out to be the body's regulator of the sleep-wake cycle — what is it?
Melatonin: Hormone released by the pineal gland.
This Russian polymath discovered the atmosphere of Venus and formulated the law of conservation of mass, while also helping shape the modern Russian literary language as a poet — who is he?
With roughly 200 species across 16 genera, this family of elongated fish is almost exclusively marine, with a name traced back through Portuguese and Latin to a Greek word — which family?
Moray eel: Family of fishes. Moray eels, or Muraenidae, are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
Sold under the brand name Revia, this medication blocks opioid receptors to reduce cravings in alcohol and opioid use disorders and is combined with bupropion to treat obesity — what is it?
Naltrexone: Medication. It has also been found to be effective for the treatment of other addictions and may be used for them off-label.
Humphry Davy coined this colorless gas's cheerful nickname for the euphoria it brings, and it still earns a spot on the WHO's Essential Medicines list for dentistry and surgery. What is it?
Nitrous oxide: Colourless non-flammable greenhouse gas.
This biological process turns a primary oocyte into an egg cell capable of developing once fertilized, beginning during embryonic development — what is it called?
Oogenesis: Egg cell production process. Oogenesis or ovogenesis is the differentiation of the ovum (egg cell) into a cell competent to further develop when fertilized.
Sold under the brand name Protonix, this proton-pump inhibitor treats ulcers and acid reflux but can, with long-term use, cause vitamin B12 deficiency and low magnesium — what is this drug?

This term for 'parts in each thousand' is symbolized by ‰ — a percent sign with an extra zero — and sits right next to the percent sign in Unicode's General Punctuation block — what is this unit called?
Per mille: Unit for parts per thousand. The associated symbol is ‰, similar to a per cent sign % but with an extra zero in the divisor.
This branch of biology studies how organs, cells, and biomolecules carry out their functions, and gives its name, alongside medicine, to a Nobel Prize category — which field?
Physiology: Science regarding functions in organisms or living systems.
Native to Southeast Asia and tasting like a sweet grapefruit, this non-hybrid citrus is the largest of them all — in fact, an ancestor of both the grapefruit and the bitter orange — what is it?
Pomelo: Citrus fruit from Southeast Asia.
Named after a Russian explorer and reintroduced to Mongolia's steppes after going extinct in the wild, this rare equine has 33 chromosome pairs instead of the usual 32 — what species is it?
Colorless and odorless, this radioactive noble gas with atomic number 86 is a decay product of radium and eventually settles into stable isotopes of lead?
Radon: Chemical element with atomic number 86 (Rn)
Made up of 12 paired bones plus the sternum and spine, this bony enclosure of the chest shields the heart and lungs while housing the muscles used for breathing — what is it?
Rib cage: Bone structure of the thorax.

Also called cot or crib death, this leading cause of infant mortality in the West strikes a baby under one, usually while sleeping between midnight and 9 a.m., and stays unexplained even after a full autopsy. What is it?
SIDS: Sudden unexplained death of a child who is less than one year of age.

Named after a colourful terrestrial flower, this predatory marine cnidarian is typically a single polyp anchored to a hard surface — a tentacled relative of coral and jellyfish, but with no medusa stage. What is it?
Sea anemone: Marine animals of the order Actiniaria.
Sitting just below carbon in group 14 of the periodic table, this blue-grey, brittle semiconductor is essential to plants and dominates the world's transistors and solar cells — which element is it?
Silicon: Chemical element with atomic number 14 (Si)
Commonly grown as an easy-care houseplant that tolerates low light, this genus of about 60 tropical species is better known by the nickname 'peace lily' — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum: Genus of plants. Certain species of Spathiphyllum are commonly known as spath or peace lilies.
Usually found in pairs and recognized as a leading cause of pneumonia since the late 19th century, which bacterium often lives harmlessly in the respiratory tracts of healthy carriers?
Streptococcus pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Streptococcus pneumoniae, or pneumococcus, is a Gram-positive, spherical bacteria, alpha-hemolytic member of the genus Streptococcus.
Marketed under the brand name Flomax, this alpha-blocker medication treats enlarged prostate symptoms and helps ease the passage of kidney stones — which drug?
Tamsulosin: Medication. Tamsulosin, sold under the brand name Flomax among others, is a medication used to treat symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis.
First unearthed in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in 1948, this Late Cretaceous giant is known mainly from claw bones over half a meter long, giving it a name meaning 'scythe lizard' — which dinosaur genus?
Therizinosaurus: Therizinosaurid genus from the Late Cretaceous period.

Famous for oversized, colorful bills nearly useless for excavation, these Neotropical birds nest in hollows dug by other animals and share an ecological niche with Africa and Asia's hornbills — what are they?
Toucan: Family of birds. The family includes five genera and over 40 different species.
Made from strained yogurt mixed with cucumber, garlic, and herbs like dill or mint, this cold Greek dip is a classic topping for souvlaki and gyros — what is it called?
Tzatziki: Cold cucumber–yogurt dip, soup, or sauce.

A hemiparasitic plant that draws water and nutrients from host trees, this species is central to European Christmas traditions and folklore, and is now studied for possible pharmaceutical use — what plant is it commonly called?
Viscum album: Flowering plant in the mistletoe family Santalaceae.
This English economist and physician first made his name surveying Irish land to parcel out to Cromwell's soldiers, and is best remembered for his theories of 'political arithmetic' — who is it?
William Petty: English economist and philosopher (1623–1687)
